title: Yesterday — the past tense
title_target: কাল আমি জাদুঘরে গেলাম — kal a-mi ja-du-ghô-ré gé-lam
goal: Tell what has already happened with the ending -লাম, and discover that the verbless sentences of Unit 1 need a verb once the story moves into the past.
bekal: form the past tense: করলাম, দেখলাম, বললাম
learn the six verbs whose stem changes: গেলাম, এলাম, খেলাম
tell the story of a past day from start to finish
use কাল, গতকাল and গত সপ্তাহে

dialogs.title: কথোপকথন — Telling about a museum visit
dialogs.intro: In the evening, Ani tells Rahim about her day over dinner. The whole dialog is in the past — watch the ending -লাম, which marks that the doer is “I”.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: Really good! We left at half past ten.
lines.literal: very — good! we — half-past — ten-o'clock-at — went.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: It was quiet in the morning. Later lots of students came.
lines.literal: morning-in — little — was. later — many — student — came.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: I saw old manuscripts, and the Ekushey photos.
lines.literal: old — manuscript — saw, and — Ekushey's — photo.

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: The Ekushey room? That's the most important one.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: I stood there a long time. My eyes filled with tears.
lines.literal: I — long-time — standing — was. eye-in — water — came.

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: Same with us. What did you have for lunch?
lines.literal: we-too — so — happen. noon-at — what — ate?

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: We had khichuri out. It was raining, you know!
lines.literal: outside-at — khichuri — ate. rain — was-happening — you-know!

lines.speaker: রহিম:
lines.id: Exactly the right food! Then where did you go?
lines.literal: totally — right — food! after-that — where — went?

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: Nowhere. We came home at half past one, and I slept for two hours!
lines.literal: anywhere — not. one-thirty-at — returned, and — two — hour — slept!

notes: **The past has four endings, and they line up with the ones you already know:** **-লাম** for আমি, **-লে** for তুমি, **-লেন** for আপনি, **-ল** for সে. করা → করলাম · করলে · করলেন · করল. দেখা → দেখলাম · দেখলে · দেখলেন · দেখল. ⚠️ Note that **-লেন** for আপনি and **-লাম** for আমি differ by just one vowel; mix them up and you're telling a story about someone else.

⚠️ **Six verbs change their stem in the past, and all are very common.** যাওয়া → **গেলাম** (not *যালাম*), আসা → **এলাম**, খাওয়া → **খেলাম**, দেওয়া → **দিলাম**, নেওয়া → **নিলাম**, পাওয়া → **পেলাম**. Learn all six as new words; no rule helps here, and learning them once lasts a lifetime.

⚠️ **The “is” that is dropped in the present comes back in the past.** আমি ছাত্র (I'm a student) → আমি ছাত্র **ছিলাম** (I was a student). এটা বই (this is a book) → এটা বই **ছিল** (this was a book). So the shortcut of Unit 1 only works in the present; once the story moves into the past, Bengali demands a full verb.

**ছিলাম is also the past of আছি.** আমি ঢাকায় আছি (I'm in Dhaka) → আমি ঢাকায় **ছিলাম** (I was in Dhaka). One form does two jobs: “was” and “was there”. ⚠️ And its negative is not নেই but **ছিলাম না** — নেই only lives in the present.

**The past progressive** combines the -ছ- infix from Unit 8 with the past endings: **করছিলাম** (I was doing), **হচ্ছিল** (was happening), **যাচ্ছিলাম** (I was on my way). It sets the scene of a story — what was going on when something else happened. ⚠️ বৃষ্টি হচ্ছিল (it was raining) versus বৃষ্টি হল (then it rained).

**Past time words you need:** **কাল** (yesterday — the verb makes it clear), **গতকাল** (yesterday, unambiguous), **গত সপ্তাহে** (last week), **গত মাসে** (last month), **আগে** (before, in the past), **তখন** (at that time). The word **গত** *gôtô* means “gone by” and goes in front of any unit of time.

⚠️ **খিচুড়ি and rain are inseparable in Bengal.** As soon as it rains, people say “খিচুড়ি খেতে ইচ্ছে করছে” (I feel like eating khichuri). It isn't superstition but a habit so strong it has become a national joke. Mention it on a rainy day and you'll sound like you've lived there for years.

grammars.title: The simple past — সাধারণ অতীত
after: **The negative is still না at the end:** আমি গেলাম না (I didn't go), সে এল না (he/she didn't come), আমি ছাত্র ছিলাম না (I wasn't a student).

grammars.title: Telling the story of a day

head: Sentence
Say it
Meaning
rows: Yesterday I got up at six.
In the morning I drank tea.
Then I went to the market.
In the afternoon I met a friend.
At night I went to bed early.
Last week I was in Dhaka.

after: ⚠️ **দেখা হল is the standard way to say “met”** — literally “a meeting happened”. Bengali often frames actions as events that happen to someone, not things someone does. This pattern comes back with more examples in Units 15 and 16.

blocks.title: একুশে ফেব্রুয়ারি — the story behind one date
items: On February 21, 1952, students in Dhaka marched to demand that Bengali be recognized as a state language. The police opened fire, and several students were killed. The event is called the **ভাষা আন্দোলন** *bhasha andolôn* — the Language Movement.
Its memorial is called the **শহীদ মিনার** *shôhid minar*. Every February 21, people walk there **barefoot** carrying flowers, singing *আমার ভাইয়ের রক্তে রাঙানো একুশে ফেব্রুয়ারি*.

⚠️ In 1999, UNESCO declared February 21 **International Mother Language Day** — the only international day born of a struggle for a language. If you're in Bengal that day, go; and dress simply, in black or white.

blocks.text: One thing about storytelling in Bengali: Bengalis value stories that are **long and full of detail**, not summaries. If someone asks “where did you go yesterday?”, a one-sentence answer feels like closing a door. Try adding one small detail — the weather, what you ate, whom you met. Your Bengali doesn't need to be perfect; what counts is your willingness to tell the story.

exercises.prompt: Change into the past for আমি.
Fill in ছিলাম, ছিলেন or ছিল.
Put the words in the right order.

items: Yesterday I went to the market.
Last week I was in Dhaka.
I used to be a student.

answers: গেলাম — খেলাম — দেখলাম — এলাম — পেলাম — বললাম
কাল আমি জাদুঘরে গেলাম। — সকালে ভিড় কম ছিল। — দুপুরে খিচুড়ি খেলাম। — তখন বৃষ্টি হচ্ছিল। — আমি দুই ঘণ্টা ঘুমালাম।
কাল আমি বাজারে গেলাম। — দুপুরে ভাত খেলাম। — তখন বৃষ্টি হচ্ছিল। — গত সপ্তাহে আমি ঢাকায় ছিলাম। — সে এল না। — আমি ছাত্র ছিলাম।
